# Self-Contained Single-File HTML

One `.html` file that renders completely with **zero outbound requests** — styles inline in a
`<style>` block, no scripts, no images, no fonts, no CDN. Copy the file anywhere, open it by
double-click, email it as an attachment: it looks the same everywhere and it works with the network
unplugged.

## The instance

`privacy-policy/index.html` in [[privacy-policy-template]]: 214 lines, one inline `<style>` block,
a two-column table of contents, 15 sections, and light/dark handled by CSS custom properties under
`@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` rather than a theme toggle. Grepped for external references,
it has **none** — every `https://` in the file is a hyperlink in the prose, never a fetched asset.
The font stack is system fonts, so nothing is downloaded to render text.

## Evidence

> "The policy is already a static site — no build step:"

> "The same policy as a self-contained, responsive web page (light/dark), ready for **GitHub Pages**"
> — privacy-policy/README.md, 2026-07-10

Both lines describe the deliverable in terms of what it *does not need*, which is the whole design
brief. See [[host-on-github-pages]] for the hosting decision it was shaped for.

## Honest scope: this is the corpus's only pure instance

Every other HTML deliverable in the source set is a *folder*, not a file:

| Candidate | Why it falls short |
|---|---|
| `Physics/exam_prep/index.html` | a 5.6 KB shell loading five `<script>` tags, a stylesheet and vendored [[katex]] — offline, but multi-file |
| `Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories/lab6_Neo4j/viewer/index.html` | 57 lines loading three `js/*` files |
| `lab4_Complexity/part2/…/index.html` | 441 lines loading six scripts |
| `lab5_GraphTheory/Q-HYDRO Wrocław` | single-page, but pulls Leaflet, tiles and Google Fonts from CDNs — the opposite property |

So the strict single-file form has **n = 1**, and this page is `confidence: medium` for that reason.
What recurs across the corpus is the weaker, more general commitment —
[[offline-first-static-deliverable]] and [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]] — of which single-file is
the extreme point rather than a separate habit. `TODO:` whether the author would reach for this
shape again, or treated it as specific to a one-page legal document, is unrecorded.

## When the extreme point is the right one

Inlining everything trades **editability for portability**, and that trade only pays when the
document is small, static and needs to survive being copied. A privacy policy is exactly that: one
page, changed a few times a year, that must render identically for a regulator, in an email
attachment, and on a Pages URL.

The cost is visible in the same repo. Because there is no generator, `PRIVACY_POLICY.md` and
`index.html` are **two hand-maintained copies of one document**. They agree today; nothing enforces
that they will. That is [[documentation-drift]] pre-loaded into the architecture — and the same
trade [[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]] makes deliberately, except here the duplication is a
side effect rather than the goal.

Above roughly one page, or the moment the content needs to be generated, the folder-shaped
deliverables in the table above are the better answer.
